title: Checkpoint: Myth and Memory
objective: After this level you can connect the land, the Bronze Age and Homer into the story of early Greece.
summary: Myths and Homer kept memories of the Bronze Age alive; archaeology and Linear B let us test them, from Knossos and Mycenae to Troy.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: Greeks kept their past in song. We check it with spades.
cards.body: Myths, epics, tablets and trenches. Put them side by side and early Greece comes into focus.

items.label: What the stories say
points: King Minos kept a monster in a Labyrinth on Crete
A Greek army besieged Troy for ten years
Agamemnon of Mycenae led the Greeks

items.label: What the evidence shows
points: A great Bronze Age palace stood at Knossos
Troy was real, and Troy VIIa fell around 1200 BCE
Mycenae’s gold mask is about 300 years too early for him

cards.headline: A memory in a helmet
cards.body: Here’s how a story can carry a real memory. The Iliad describes a helmet covered in boar’s tusks. Archaeologists have found helmets like that in Mycenaean-era graves, from centuries before Homer. The palaces burned and writing was lost, but a piece of Bronze Age gear survived in song. Mycenaean culture left a lasting mark on later Greek myth and epic.

cards.headline: One story
cards.body: Put Chapter 1 together. Mountains split Greece apart, and the sea opened it up. Palace kingdoms rose on Crete and then on the mainland, keeping records on clay. Around 1200 BCE they fell, and writing went with them. Singers kept the old stories alive in performance, until an alphabet borrowed from the Phoenicians let Greeks write again, and colonists carried Greek cities around the sea.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: How myths and Homer's poems kept memories of Bronze Age Greece alive, and how archaeology tests them.
Why mountains split Greece into separate valleys, while the sea became the easiest road.
What the palace kingdoms of Crete and Mycenae left behind, from painted walls to clay record tablets.
Why Greece lost writing when the palaces fell, and how a borrowed alphabet with vowels brought it back.

questions.prompt: Myth and Memory recap: what did cracking the Linear B tablets reveal about the Mycenaeans?

options.label: They wrote an early form of Greek
They wrote the same script as the Minoans
options.rationale: Minoan Linear A is still unread.

options.label: They recorded the whole story of Troy
They wrote in Phoenician letters

questions.explanation: Ventris showed in 1952 that Linear B recorded an early form of Greek, mostly palace inventories.

questions.prompt: Looking back on Homer in Myth and Memory: what is the “Homeric question”?

options.label: Whether Troy existed at all
Whether the Iliad came before the Odyssey
Whether one poet or many made the epics
Whether Homer wrote in Linear B

questions.explanation: Some scholars think one poet composed both epics; others think many people retold and revised them. It’s still open.

questions.prompt: How does the boar’s tusk helmet suggest that Homer’s poems kept real Bronze Age memories?

options.label: It was found in Homer’s own grave
options.rationale: No grave of Homer is known.

options.label: It carries a Linear B label naming Odysseus
Homer describes a helmet type found in Mycenaean graves
It was made after the Iliad as a stage prop

questions.explanation: The Iliad describes a boar’s tusk helmet, a type found in Mycenaean-era graves from centuries before Homer.

questions.prompt: In Myth and Memory’s story-versus-evidence check, what does archaeology add to the Troy legend?

options.label: Proof that Achilles really lived
A real city that fell around 1200 BCE
Nothing, since no ruins survive
Proof the siege lasted ten years

questions.explanation: Troy was real, and Troy VIIa was destroyed around 1200 BCE, though the ten-year siege is unproven.

questions.prompt: Myth and Memory recap: which order of early Greek writing is right?

options.label: Dark Age with no writing, Linear B palaces, Phoenician alphabet
Phoenician alphabet, Linear B palaces, Dark Age
Linear B palaces, Phoenician alphabet, Dark Age
options.rationale: The Dark Age came before the alphabet.

options.label: Linear B palaces, Dark Age with no writing, Phoenician alphabet

questions.explanation: Palaces kept Linear B records until about 1200 BCE; writing was lost in the Dark Age; then Greeks borrowed the Phoenician alphabet.
